brief: Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities daily note covering five subjects. GS expects August core CPI at 0.23% against 0.2% consensus and 2.40% year over year, after hotter PPI in hospitals and airfares led GIR to lift core PCE by 2bps. The argument: 0.25 on core is the September dividing line, the Fed will do what the market guides towards, and with 35-50% of a hike priced post-CPI, not hiking would be punitive for the back end, so a modestly higher 0.26-0.28 print may be cleaner because it forces full September pricing rather than adding hikes, with almost 90bps priced to Dec 27. Oracle cloud infrastructure revenue rose 121% to $7.4bn with RPO at $664bn and GPU utilization at 97.9%, read by the desk as compute staying scarce and pricing strong. Microsoft plans to more than triple data center capacity to above 38GW by 2032. Houthi seizure of Mocha and advance to the Hanish Islands raises Bab el-Mandeb leverage, with a 25% chance of closure by December priced on Polymarket. The top 10 requested consumer meetings average 32% off 52-week highs versus SPY at 2.7%, and the desk expects a better tone than price action suggests.
